text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Wednesday morning newspapers:
- Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi, who held his first official visit to Slovenia on Tuesday, said Italy strongly supported Slovenia's bids for membership of NATO and the European Union.
- A Slovenian astronomer discovered two new asteroids.
- The Slovenian Tax Office last year discovered tax evasions totalling four billion tolars ($25.6 million).
- Organisers of the final ski-jumping world cup competition of the season, scheduled at Planica on March 20 to 23, said the competition would take place despite a lack of snow.

- Slovenian basketball team Smelt Olimpija won a Euroleague match against Croatia's Cibona by 69 to 66, thus equalling the standing. The final game between the two teams will take place in Zagreb on Thursday.

- The council of the Christian Democratic Party (SKD) does not accept the resignation of the party's leadership despite poor November election performance when SKD only got 10 parliamentary seats, down from 15 four years ago.
- Private telecommunication companies are pushing for a change in the telecommunications law which currently allows state mobile phone operator Mobitel to monopolise the sector.
- The police union said it might prepare a strike if the government fails to improve work conditions and salaries.
- Car maker Revoz, the Slovenian partner of France's Renault, said Renault's drive to lower expenses is not likely to have any negative influence on Revoz.
- The Slovenian branch of France's car maker Citroen said sales in Slovenia rose to 599 cars in the first two months of 1997, up from 150 in the same period last year.
